headline: Cannabis week ahead: DEA stay ruling due before 29 November
dek: The D.C. Circuit has a short, holiday-broken week to rule on pausing the DEA's 29 November supply-chain deadline, as Bedrocan and Russell dates also land.
key_points: The government's answer to the first emergency stay motion against the DEA's supply-chain guidance is due at the D.C. Circuit by 4 p.m. Eastern on Monday 23 November, with the companies' reply due a day later.
The court is closed on 26 and 27 November for Thanksgiving, which leaves two working days after the reply for a ruling before the Sunday 29 November deadline.

IM Cannabis expects its 3-for-1 share consolidation to take effect around 23 November, Rhode Island's retail licence portal closes the same day, and FTSE Russell updates its preliminary index lists on 27 November.
The Dutch parliament debates the Bedrocan collapse on 26 November, and Minnesota's medical licensees face a 4 December attestation deadline before the state merges its supply chains.
body: Thanksgiving week is usually quiet for cannabis policy. This one is not. The most consequential date is not on the holiday at all: it is Sunday 29 November, when the DEA expects medical cannabis businesses waiting on federal registration to trade only with other registrants or applicants. Seven companies in four states have asked a federal appeals court to pause that expectation, and the court has built itself a tight timetable to decide.

Below is MetaFlora's calendar for 23 to 30 November, with the dates that follow into early December. Every date comes from a court, regulator, company release or the reporting linked at the end. Times are local to each event.
## Monday 23 November: the DEA answers

As we reported on 21 November, a special panel of the U.S. Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit ordered the government to respond to the first emergency stay motion by 4 p.m. Eastern on Monday. The companies may reply by 4 p.m. on Tuesday 24 November. The two petitions, No. 26-1324 brought by operators in Utah, Arizona and Oklahoma and No. 26-1325 brought by four Pennsylvania grower-processors, were consolidated on 19 November.

The government's filing is the first time the DEA will have to defend in court the guidance it published on 30 October. That guidance tells businesses that applied for registration in the window from 28 April to 26 June to restructure their supply chains by 29 November so they deal only with registrants or other timely applicants. The Pennsylvania companies say they registered their dispensaries in time but not their own manufacturing, and that from 29 November their cultivation arms could not lawfully supply their own stores. By Sunday 22 November we had seen no report of a ruling on either motion.

The same morning, IM Cannabis expects its three-for-one share consolidation to take effect, subject to Nasdaq's confirmation, according to the company's 18 November release. Its outstanding shares would fall from about 1.84 million to about 615,000. Because the company already carried out a 30-for-1 consolidation on 27 August, it says it does not qualify for Nasdaq's usual 180-day grace period: if its closing bid stays under US$1.00 for 30 consecutive business days, Nasdaq staff would issue a delisting determination. Ronen Zalayet took over as chief executive on 19 November.
In Rhode Island, the Cannabis Control Commission's portal for new adult-use retail licence applications closes at 4 p.m. Eastern, according to The Marijuana Herald.
> The DEA's deadline lands on a Sunday after a two-day court closure. Any stay has to come by Wednesday or it comes after the fact.
## Wednesday 25 to Friday 27 November: a holiday with a hole in it

Wednesday is Green Wednesday, the busiest pre-holiday sales day for many US dispensaries. Thursday is Thanksgiving. The D.C. Circuit's own notice says the court is closed on Thursday 26 and Friday 27 November. Electronic filing stays open, and anything due on those two days is treated as filed on time on the next day the court opens. In practice, on our reading of the timetable, that leaves Tuesday evening and Wednesday 25 November as the window for the panel to act before the deadline, unless it rules over the weekend.

Across the Atlantic, the Tweede Kamer, the lower house of the Dutch parliament, is due to debate the bankruptcy of Bedrocan Nederland on Thursday 26 November, according to Business of Cannabis. As we reported on 20 November, the court-appointed trustees' first report traces the collapse to the state buyer's refusal to take delivery of stock it had ordered, which cuts against the health minister's account. The same day in London, Richard List, the police drugs adviser who wrote the national guidance on medical cannabis patients, speaks at the Cannabis Health London Symposium; we cover his plans in a separate story this evening.

On Friday 27 November, FTSE Russell publishes the next update to the preliminary lists for its December reconstitution, according to LSEG. Trulieve and Glass House Brands were on the first preliminary list of Russell 3000 additions, IgniteIt reported. Further updates follow on 4 December, and the new indexes take effect after the US market close on 11 December.
## Sunday 29 November: the deadline

If no stay is granted, the DEA's supply-chain expectation applies from Sunday. The guidance is not a regulation, and the agency has described it as information for applicants, but it warns that dealing outside the circle of registrants and timely applicants could count against an application. For vertically integrated operators that registered only part of their business, the practical choice is between stopping internal transfers and risking their federal application. State regulators have said little: as we reported on 19 November, Massachusetts told its licensees it had no federal guidance of its own to offer.
## Monday 30 November and into December

Missouri's rules licensing marijuana research facilities, 19 CSR 100-1.200, take effect on 30 November, according to The Marijuana Herald. The same day is the contract-change date for the US Department of Agriculture's revised hemp crop insurance provisions for 2027, which we covered on 19 November.

On 1 December, new Connecticut provisions on manufacturing cannabinoids such as CBG and CBN in the licensed market take effect, the Herald reported. Minnesota adds new tracking categories for high-medical-need products the same day, and its medical licensees must file an attestation with the Office of Cannabis Management by 4 December ahead of the state's 1 January supply-chain merger. North Carolina's governor-appointed cannabis council has 1 December as the target for circulating its internal draft, with a vote on the final report targeted for 15 December, the Winston-Salem Chronicle reported.

Also on 4 December, Los Angeles holds its retail storefront lottery, and Curaleaf's bid for Aurora Cannabis is set to expire unless extended, as we reported on 16 November. DEA comments on 2027 production quotas close on 10 December. On 11 December the remaining federal hemp definition changes, including the 0.4-milligram total THC cap per container, take effect.
## What to watch

The D.C. Circuit order is the only event this week that could change how hundreds of state-licensed medical businesses operate on Monday 30 November. Watch the government's filing on 23 November for whether the DEA offers any flexibility, such as a later date or a carve-out for integrated operators, which could make a court order unnecessary. Watch IM Cannabis's first trading days after consolidation against the US$1.00 line. And watch whether Dutch MPs press for the 2025 settlement between Bedrocan and the state buyer to be disclosed.
